channel.title: AI Stupa Translation Project
channel.description: New English translations of texts from the Tibetan Buddhist canon, made by the AI Stupa (provisional, public domain).

item.title: The Noble Great Vehicle Sūtra "The White Lotus of Great Compassion" (Toh 111)
item.description: The White Lotus of Great Compassion, known in Sanskrit as the Ārya Mahākaruṇāpuṇḍarīka Mahāyāna Sūtra and in Tibetan as Pakpa Nyingjé Chenpo'i Padma Karpo, is a Great Vehicle discourse set at the most solemn moment of the Buddha's life. It opens in the sāla grove of the Mallas near Kuśinagara, where the Blessed One tells the venerable Ānanda that he will pass into complete nirvāṇa in the last…

item.title: The Noble Great Vehicle Sūtra Called The Teaching on the Magical Display in the Domain of Skillful Means within the Bodhisattva's Sphere of Activity (Toh 146)
item.description: The Teaching on the Magical Display in the Domain of Skillful Means within the Bodhisattva's Sphere of Activity, known in Sanskrit as the Ārya Bodhisattvagocaropāyaviṣayavikurvaṇanirdeśa and in Tibetan as Phakpa Jangchup Sempé Chöyul gyi Tabkyi Yul la Nampar Trulpa Tenpa, is a Great Vehicle sūtra found as Toh 146 in the Kangyur, in its General Sūtra section. Set in the pleasure garden of King…

item.title: The Noble Great Vehicle Sūtra Called The Questions of Gaganagañja (Toh 148)
item.description: The Noble Great Vehicle Sūtra called The Questions of Gaganagañja, known in Sanskrit as the Āryagaganagañjaparipṛcchā and in Tibetan as Phakpa Namkha Dzö Kyi Zhüpa, is a Mahāyāna sūtra in which the bodhisattva Gaganagañja questions the Buddha in a vast jeweled assembly about the conduct, qualities and wisdom of bodhisattvas. In the course of the discourse the Buddha praises above all the…

item.title: The Noble Mahāyāna Sūtra Called Conformity with the World (Toh 200)
item.description: The Noble Mahāyāna Sūtra Called Conformity with the World, known in Sanskrit as the Lokānuvartana Sūtra and in Tibetan as 'Phags pa 'jig rten gyi rjes su 'thun par 'jug pa zhes bya ba theg pa chen po'i mdo, is a short Mahāyāna discourse composed entirely in verse. Requested by Mañjughoṣa for the sake of beings in times to come, the Buddha explains that the buddhas are wholly beyond the world…

item.title: The Noble Great Vehicle Sūtra Called Benefiting Aṅgulimāla (Toh 213)
item.description: The Noble Great Vehicle Sūtra called Benefiting Aṅgulimāla, known in Sanskrit as the Āryāṅgulimālīya Mahāyāna Sūtra and in Tibetan as Phakpa Sormo Trengwa la Penpa, is a Mahāyāna sūtra set at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, where the Buddha teaches a vast assembly of bodhisattvas, monastics, and gods and spirits of every kind. It takes up the famous story of Aṅgulimāla, the killer who wore a garland…

item.title: The Pledge of the Tathāgata's Glory (Toh 230)
item.description: The Pledge of the Tathāgata's Glory, known in Sanskrit as the Tathāgataśrīsamaya and in Tibetan as De bzhin gshegs pa'i dpal gyi dam tshig, is a Great Vehicle sūtra that presents itself as belonging to the Great Assembly, the Mahāsannipāta, a large collection of Mahāyāna discourses. It opens in the classic sūtra manner, with the Buddha dwelling on a mountain described as the abode of sages…

item.title: The Excerpt of the Chapter on Māra from the Ninth Fascicle of the Great Uṣṇīṣa (Toh 237)
item.description: The Excerpt of the Chapter on Māra from the Ninth Fascicle of the Great Uṣṇīṣa, known in Tibetan as Tsuktor Chenpo Bampo Gupa Lé Dü kyi Le'u Nyitsé Chungwa, is a short sūtra extract drawn from a scripture referred to as the Great Uṣṇīṣa (in Sanskrit, Mahoṣṇīṣa), which corresponds to the Chinese Śūraṅgama Sūtra, and early Tibetan catalogues record that it was translated from Chinese. In it the…

item.title: The Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha, a Great Vehicle Sūtra from the Great Collection (Toh 239)
item.description: The Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha, known in Sanskrit as the Daśacakrakṣitigarbha Sūtra and in Tibetan as Sai Nyingpö Khorlo Chupa, is a Great Vehicle sūtra presented as part of the Great Collection, the vast Mahāyāna compilation of discourses. Set on Mount Khaladeya, where the Buddha dwells with great assemblies of monks and bodhisattvas, it tells how the bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha arrives amid wondrous…

item.title: The Noble Great Vehicle Sūtra Called The Irreversible Wheel (Toh 240)
item.description: The Noble Great Vehicle Sūtra called The Irreversible Wheel, known in Sanskrit as the Āryāvaivartacakra and in Tibetan as Phakpa Chir Mi Dokpé Khorlo, is a Mahāyāna sūtra preserved as Toh 240 in the Kangyur, where it belongs to the General Sūtra section. It opens at Śrāvastī, in the Jeta Grove, where the Buddha, the youthful Mañjuśrī, and the bodhisattva Maitreya each enter deep meditative…

item.title: The Noble Great Vehicle Sūtra Called "The Wheel of Dedication" (Toh 242)
item.description: The Noble Great Vehicle Sūtra called "The Wheel of Dedication," known in Sanskrit as the Ārya Pariṇatacakra Nāma Mahāyāna Sūtra and in Tibetan as Pakpa Yongsu Ngowé Khorlo, is a short Mahāyāna sūtra found as Toh 242 in the Kangyur, among the general sūtras. Set on the summit of a jewel-and-vajra mountain, it records the Buddha teaching the bodhisattva Vajraratna a liturgy for those who wish to…

item.title: The Five Thousand Four Hundred and Fifty-Three Names of the Buddha (Toh 262)
item.description: The Five Thousand Four Hundred and Fifty-Three Names of the Buddha, known in Sanskrit as the Buddhanāmasahasrapañcaśatacaturtripañcadaśa and in Tibetan as Sangyé kyi Tsen Ngatong Zhigya Ngachu Tsasumpa, is Toh 262 in the Kangyur, where it belongs to the General Sūtra section. It is a devotional sūtra made up almost entirely of a long litany of homages, each one paying respect to a tathāgata by…

item.title: The Noble Mahāyāna Sūtra Called The Array of the Great Liberation That Extends in All Directions (Toh 264)
item.description: The Noble Mahāyāna Sūtra Called The Array of the Great Liberation That Extends in All Directions, in Which Wrongdoing Is Purified by Repentance and Buddhahood Is Attained, known in Tibetan as Tharpa Chenpo Chok su Gyepa, is Toh 264 in the Kangyur, where it belongs to the General Sūtra section. Unlike most texts in the collection, it carries no Sanskrit title, because it was translated into…

item.title: The Sūtra of the Renunciation (Toh 301)
item.description: The Sūtra of the Renunciation, known in Sanskrit as the Abhiniṣkramaṇa Sūtra and in Tibetan as Ngönpar Jungwé Do, is a narrative sūtra on the life and lineage of the Buddha, centered on his going forth from household life in pursuit of awakening. It opens with verses of homage to the Three Jewels, praising the Buddha for his boundless generosity in former lives, and goes on to tell the story of…

item.title: The Sūtra Called the Wise and the Foolish (Toh 341)
item.description: The Sūtra Called the Wise and the Foolish, known in Tibetan as Dzanglun, is Toh 341 in the Kangyur, where it is placed in the General Sūtra section. Unlike most canonical sūtras it has no Sanskrit title line, and its own colophon notes that it appears to have been translated from Chinese; it corresponds to a collection compiled in Central Asia from stories heard by Chinese monks, and the Sanskrit…

item.title: The Hundred Avadānas Beginning with Pūrṇa (Toh 343)
item.description: The Hundred Avadānas Beginning with Pūrṇa, known in Sanskrit as the Avadānaśataka and in Tibetan as Gang po la sogs pa'i rtogs pa brjod pa brgya pa, is a great collection of one hundred avadānas, or stories of noble deeds, illustrating how actions bear fruit across lifetimes. Grouped in decades, each introduced by a short summary verse, its tales tell of brahmins, merchants, kings, gods, and…

item.title: The Sūtra of the Great Skillful Means by Which the Buddha's Kindness Is Repaid (Toh 353)
item.description: The Great Skillful Means by Which the Buddha Repays Kindness, in Tibetan Tabkhepa Chenpo Sangyé Drinlen Sabpé Do, is a Mahāyāna discourse that was translated into Tibetan from Chinese rather than Sanskrit, and so it carries a Chinese title in place of the usual Sanskrit one. Set on Vulture Peak near Rājagṛha before a vast assembly of monks and bodhisattvas, it unfolds over nine chapters on how…

item.title: The Noble Sūtra in Forty-Two Sections (Toh 359a)
item.description: The Noble Sūtra Called Forty-Two Sections, known in Tibetan as Phakpa Dumbu Zhenyipa Zhejawé Do, is the Tibetan version of the Chinese Sūtra in Forty-two Sections, and its title line gives the Chinese name in Tibetan transcription instead of a Sanskrit one. The sūtra opens just after the Buddha's awakening, when he turns the wheel of the Dharma of the four truths for the group of five at the Deer…

item.title: The Higher Tantra of the Abhidhāna (Toh 369)
item.description: The Higher Tantra of the Abhidhāna, known in Sanskrit as the Abhidhānottara Tantra and in Tibetan as Ngönpar Jöpé Gyü Lama, is a scripture of the Cakrasaṃvara cycle of Buddhist tantra, opening with homage to glorious Vajraḍāka and set among the wrathful vajra beings, ḍākas and ḍākinīs of all the tathāgatas. Over many chapters it presents the deities of the Heruka and Cakrasaṃvara maṇḍalas, their…

item.title: The Great King of Yoginī Tantras called the Glorious Ocean of Ḍākas (Toh 372)
item.description: The Great King of Yoginī Tantras called the Glorious Ocean of Ḍākas, known in Sanskrit as the Śrī Ḍākārṇava Mahāyoginī Tantrarāja and in Tibetan as Pal Khandro Gyatso Naljorma'i Gyü kyi Gyalpo Chenpo, is Toh 372 in the Kangyur, where it belongs to the Tantra section among the yoginī tantras associated with the Cakrasaṃvara cycle. It opens in the manner of a sūtra, with the Blessed One, the Lord…

item.title: The Great King of Tantras Called the Arising of Glorious Saṃvara (Toh 373)
item.description: The Great King of Tantras Called the Arising of Glorious Saṃvara, known in Sanskrit as the Śrī Mahāsaṃvarodaya Tantrarāja and in Tibetan as Pal Demchok Jungwa, is one of the principal explanatory tantras of the Cakrasaṃvara cycle, a yoginī tantra centered on the deity Heruka. Framed as a dialogue in which Vajrapāṇi questions the Blessed One, its thirty-three chapters address the yogas of the…

item.title: The Great King of Tantras (Toh 442)
item.description: The Great King of Tantras, the Great Secret of the Body, Speech, and Mind of All Tathāgatas, Called the Guhyasamāja, known in Sanskrit as the Sarvatathāgatakāyavākcittarahasya Guhyasamāja and in Tibetan as Sangwa Düpa, the "Secret Assembly," is one of the most influential scriptures of Indian and Tibetan Vajrayāna Buddhism. Taught by the Buddha while dwelling in the secret abode of the vajra…

item.title: The Great Yoga Tantra, the Explanatory Tantra of the Glorious Vajra Garland, the Analysis of the Secret Essence of All Tantras (Toh 445)
item.description: The Explanatory Tantra of the Glorious Vajra Garland, the Analysis of the Secret Essence of All Tantras, known in Sanskrit as the Śrī Vajramālābhidhāna Mahāyoga Tantra Sarvatantrahṛdayarahasyavibhaṅga and in Tibetan as the Palden Dorjé Trengwa, or Vajra Garland, is a great yoga tantra in which the Blessed One, the essence of the body, speech, and mind of all the tathāgatas, answers the questions…

item.title: The King of Tantras (Toh 449)
item.description: The King of Tantras, the Later Tantra from the Ultimate Assembly, the Source of All Activities, known in Sanskrit as the Samāja Paramārtha Sarvakarmodaya Uttaratantrarāja and in Tibetan as Phrin las thams cad 'byung ba 'dus pa don dam pa las phyi ma'i rgyud kyi rgyal po, is Toh 449 in the Kangyur, where it belongs to the Tantra section among the yoginī tantras devoted to the goddess Tārā. It is a…

item.title: The Great King of Tantras called Glorious Candraguhyatilaka (Toh 477)
item.description: The Great King of Tantras called Glorious Candraguhyatilaka, in Sanskrit Śrī Candraguhyatilaka Mahātantrarāja and in Tibetan Dpal zla gsang thig le, is a Buddhist tantra whose title may be rendered "the Secret Drop of the Moon." It is Toh 477 in the Kangyur, where it belongs to the Tantra section among the higher yoga tantras. Opening with a homage to Vajrasattva, it unfolds as a dialogue in…

item.title: The King of Tantras Called the Glorious Red Yamāri (Toh 478)
item.description: The King of Tantras Called the Glorious Red Yamāri, known in Sanskrit as the Śrī Raktayamāri Tantrarāja and in Tibetan as Palden Shinjé Shepa Marpö Gyü kyi Gyalpo, is a Buddhist tantra devoted to Red Yamāri, the red, wrathful form of Yamāntaka, the conqueror of death. Framed as a dialogue in which the Blessed One, embraced by his consort, answers her requests for the sake of beings, it presents…

item.title: The Great Vehicle Sūtra Called the Compendium of the Reality of All Tathāgatas (Toh 479)
item.description: The Compendium of the Reality of All Tathāgatas, known in Sanskrit as the Sarvatathāgatatattvasaṃgraha and in Tibetan as De bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi de kho na nyid bsdus pa, is a foundational scripture of Buddhist yoga tantra that presents itself as a Great Vehicle sūtra. Set in the Akaniṣṭha heaven, it describes how the Blessed One Vairocana, endowed with the blessing of all the tathāgatas…

item.title: The Vajra Peak, the Tantra of the Great Secret Yoga (Toh 480)
item.description: The Vajra Peak, the Tantra of the Great Secret Yoga, known in Sanskrit as the Vajraśikhara Mahāguhyayoga Tantra and in Tibetan as Sangwa Naljor Chenpo'i Gyü Dorjé Tsemo, is Toh 480 in the Kangyur, where it belongs to the Tantra section among the scriptures of the yoga tantra class. Opening with homage to Samantabhadra, to all the tathāgatas and to the Tathāgata Vairocana, it presents the buddhas…

item.title: The Section of the Mantra Ritual of Śrī Paramādya (Toh 488)
item.description: The Section of the Mantra Ritual of Śrī Paramādya, known in Sanskrit as the Śrī Paramādya Mantra Kalpa Khaṇḍa and in Tibetan as Pal Chok Dangpö Ngak kyi Tokpé Dumbu, is a tantra devoted to the cycle of Paramādya, the Glorious Supreme Primordial One, a form of Vajrasattva identified with great bliss. Opening with Vairocana teaching the Pledge of the Unfailing Vajra of Great Bliss as a gateway to…

item.title: The Glorious Ornament of the Vajra Essence, Great King of Tantras (Toh 490)
item.description: The Glorious Ornament of the Vajra Essence, Great King of Tantras, known in Sanskrit as the Śrī Vajramaṇḍālaṃkāra Mahātantrarāja and in Tibetan as Pal Dorjé Nyingpo Gyen, is Toh 490 in the Kangyur, where it belongs to the Tantra section among the tantras of the yoga class. It opens in the manner of a sūtra, with the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Body, Speech and Mind Vajra, presiding over an…

item.title: The Manifest Awakening of the Great Vairocana: The Extensive Blessing of Its Manifestations, a Dharma Discourse Called the King of the Lords of Sūtras (Toh 494)
item.description: The Manifest Awakening of the Great Vairocana, known in Sanskrit as the Mahāvairocanābhisaṃbodhi and in Tibetan as Nampar Nangdzé Chenpo Ngönpar Dzokpar Changchupa, is one of the foundational scriptures of esoteric Buddhism, presented in its full title as an extensive discourse on the manifestations and blessing of Vairocana's perfect awakening, a king among sūtras. It is Toh 494 in the Kangyur…

item.title: The Ritual Manual Teaching the Taming of the Valiant through the Immeasurable Power of All the Tathāgatas, of Noble Acala, King of the Wrathful Ones (Toh 495)
item.description: The Ritual Manual of Noble Acala, King of the Wrathful Ones, Taught for the Taming of the Valiant through the Immeasurable Power of All the Tathāgatas, known in Sanskrit as the Āryācalamahākrodharājasya Sarvatathāgatasya Balāparimitavīravinayasvākhyāto Nāma Kalpa and in Tibetan as De bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi khro bo'i rgyal po 'phags pa mi g.yo ba de'i stobs dpag tu med pa rtul phod pa 'dul…

item.title: The Great Tantra of the Empowerment of Noble Vajrapāṇi (Toh 496)
item.description: The Great Tantra of the Empowerment of Noble Vajrapāṇi, known in Sanskrit as the Āryavajrapāṇyabhiṣekamahātantra and in Tibetan as Pakpa Lakna Dorjé Wangkurwé Gyü Chenpo, is a lengthy scripture of the tantra class, catalogued as Toh 496 in the Kangyur, where it is placed among the tantras of the action (kriyā) class. It opens in the great palace of Vaśavartin, king of the gods, where the Blessed…

item.title: The Tantra Called the King of the Array of the Three Pledges (Toh 502)
item.description: The King of the Array of the Three Pledges, known in Sanskrit as the Trisamayavyūharāja Tantra and in Tibetan as Damtsik Sum Köpé Gyalpo, is a Buddhist tantra preserved as Toh 502 in the Kangyur, where it belongs to the Tantra section among the scriptures of action tantra (kriyā tantra). Set in the great vajra palace of the dharmadhātu, where the tathāgatas and the great vajra holders gather, it…

item.title: The Secret Tantra of the Ritual Manual of Krodhavijaya (Toh 604)
item.description: The Secret Tantra of the Ritual Manual of Krodhavijaya, known in Sanskrit as the Krodhavijayakalpaguhyatantra and in Tibetan as Khro bo rnam par rgyal ba'i rtog pa gsang ba'i rgyud, is a tantric scripture centered on Yamāntaka, the wrathful form of the bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, here called Krodhavijaya, the Victorious Wrathful One. It opens with the terrifying appearance of this wrathful deity…

item.title: The Dhāraṇī Given by the Nāgas, called The Heart of the Nāgas (Toh 685)
item.description: The Dhāraṇī Given by the Nāgas, called The Heart of the Nāgas, in Sanskrit Nāgadattadhāraṇī Nāgahṛdaya and in Tibetan Lü Jinpé Zung Lü Nyingpo, is a short dhāraṇī text catalogued as Toh 685 in the Kangyur, in its Tantra section. After a brief verse promising that whoever recites this knowledge mantra, spoken by the Buddha, will have nothing to fear from the nāgas, it consists almost entirely of…

item.title: The Great Ritual Manual of Ūrdhvajaṭā, from the Vast Chapters on the Miraculous Display of the Great Bodhisattva: The Root Manual of the Blessed Lady, Noble Tārā (Toh 724)
item.description: The Great Ritual Manual of Ūrdhvajaṭā, known in Sanskrit as the Ūrdhvajaṭā Mahākalpa and more fully as the Root Manual of the Blessed Lady, Noble Tārā (Āryatārā Mūlakalpa), and in Tibetan as Ralpa Gyendzé kyi Tokpa Chenpo, presents itself as drawn from the Vast Chapters on the Miraculous Display of the Great Bodhisattva. It is Toh 724 in the Kangyur, where it belongs to the Tantra section among…

item.title: The Great Perfection of All Phenomena (Toh 828)
item.description: The Great Perfection of All Phenomena, the All-Creating King, the Awakening Mind, known in Tibetan as Kunjé Gyalpo and given a Sanskrit title rendered in the text as Sarva Dharma Mahā Santi Bodhi Citta Kulaya Rājā, is Toh 828 in the Kangyur, where it stands among the Ancient, or Nyingma, tantras. It is the principal scripture of the Mind Class of the Great Perfection, a tantra set in the realm of…

item.title: The Sūtra Called the Tantra of the Vajra Array, the Essence of the Meaning of the Secret Wisdom of the Mind of All the Tathāgatas; the Scripture of Accomplishment in Yoga; the Sūtra of the Knowledge That Gathers All; the Discourse of Dharma That Arrays the Clear Realization of the Great Vehicle (Toh 829)
item.description: The Sūtra of the Gathering of the Intentions of All Buddhas, known in Tibetan as Sangyé Kungyi Gongpa Düpé Do and often simply as the Gongpa Düpa, bears a long Sanskrit title beginning Sarvatathāgatacittajñānaguhyārthagarbhavyūhavajratantra, which presents it at once as a vajra tantra, a scripture of accomplishment in yoga, a sūtra that gathers all knowledge, and a discourse arraying the clear…

item.title: The Noble Dhāraṇī That Dispels Obstructors (Toh 959)
item.description: The Noble Dhāraṇī That Dispels Obstructors, known in Tibetan as Pakpa Gek Selwé Zung and given in its Sanskrit title line as Ārya Vighna Vināyaka Dhāraṇī, is a short incantation text centered on the deity Gaṇapati, the remover and lord of obstacles. Set at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, it records the Buddha teaching the venerable Nanda that whoever holds Gaṇapati's heart mantra will succeed in…

item.title: The Noble Averter Called the Powerful One (Toh 960)
item.description: The Noble Averter Called the Powerful One, known in Sanskrit as Ārya Balavatī Nāma Pratyaṅgirā, is a short protective dhāraṇī text whose Tibetan title carries the same meaning. It opens with homage to the Three Jewels and to the bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, praised for his great compassion and love toward all beings. It then presents an averting spell to be recited for the protection of life and…

item.title: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called Vanquishing Bandits (Toh 961)
item.description: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called Vanquishing Bandits, known in Sanskrit as the Āryacauravidhvaṃsana Nāma Dhāraṇī, is a brief protective incantation whose Tibetan title is given in the text as an equivalent rendering of that name. The text opens as the Buddha sets out from Mount Videha with his attendant Ānanda, who catches sight of a large band of robbers in the distance and is struck with terror. The…

item.title: Homage to the Blessed One, Blazing Uṣṇīṣa (Toh 962)
item.description: The Blazing Uṣṇīṣa Dhāraṇī, known in Tibetan as Tsuktor Barwa and in Sanskrit roughly as the Uṣṇīṣa Jvala, is a very short incantation text that opens with homage to the Blessed One, Blazing Uṣṇīṣa, the radiant crown protuberance of a buddha personified as a deity. After the homage it gives a single mantra, addressed to all the buddhas whose teaching is unobstructed, that calls on the deity to…

item.title: The Noble Dhāraṇī of the Wrathful One Acala (Toh 963)
item.description: The Noble Dhāraṇī of the Wrathful One Acala, known in Sanskrit as the Āryācala­nāma­dhāraṇī and in Tibetan as ʼphags pa khro bo mi g.yo ba, is a short dhāraṇī text centered on Acala, the "Immovable One," a fierce protective deity. After paying homage to the Three Jewels, it vividly describes Acala's form. He has the body of a man in the prime of youth and is dark as summer rain clouds. He blazes…

item.title: The Vajra Beak, the Commitment of the Nāgas (Toh 964)
item.description: The Vajra Beak, the Commitment of the Nāgas, known in Sanskrit as Vajratuṇḍa Nāma Nāgasamaya and in Tibetan as Dorje Chu Zhejawa Lui Damtsik, is a ritual scripture concerned with the nāgas, the serpent-like beings of Buddhist cosmology associated with water, weather, and disease. It opens with the Buddha teaching in the great city of Gyokdor before a vast assembly of nāgas, led by figures such as…

item.title: The Dhāraṇī Called Vajra Meteoric Iron Beak (Toh 965)
item.description: The Dhāraṇī Called Vajra Meteoric Iron Beak, known in Sanskrit as the Vajralohatuṇḍanāmadhāraṇī and in Tibetan as Dorje Namchak Chu zhe jawai zung, is a short protective incantation addressed to the dangers posed by hostile nāgas and destructive weather. It opens with the gods Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara, together with the Four Great Kings, circling the Blessed One and asking him to bless a…

item.title: The Noble Black Iron Beak (Toh 966)
item.description: The Noble Black Iron Beak, known in Sanskrit as Ārya Kṛṣṇāyoṣṭha and in Tibetan as Phakpa Chakchu Nakpo, is a short scripture presented as a discourse of the Buddha, opening with the familiar words "Thus did I hear at one time." It describes the Blessed One staying in a reed thicket at a place where boats come to rest, then setting out with the venerable Ānanda for a place in Jambudvīpa. There…

item.title: The Noble Sūtra Called Taking Back Vitality (Toh 967)
item.description: The Noble Sūtra Called Taking Back Vitality, known in Sanskrit as the Ārya Ojaḥpratyaṃgiraṇa Sūtra and in Tibetan as Pakpa Dang Chirtrokpa Zhejawé Do, is a short protective scripture centered on a spell for safeguarding a person's life force. Set at Śrāvastī, it opens with the Buddha urging the venerable Ānanda to take up, hold, read, and fully master the vidyā-mantra of Taking Back Vitality. He…

item.title: The Noble Victorious Averter (Toh 968)
item.description: The Noble Victorious Averter, known in Sanskrit as Āryavijayavatī nāma Pratyaṅgirā, is a short protective scripture whose Tibetan title carries the same meaning of a victorious spell that turns back harm. It opens with homage to all the buddhas and bodhisattvas who strive to protect beings, to the accomplished ones and the holders of spell-mantras, to the Three Jewels, and to the great…

item.title: The Noble King of Vidyā-Mantras Called "Great Breath" (Toh 969)
item.description: The Noble King of Vidyā-Mantras Called "Great Breath" is a short scripture whose Tibetan title opens with the words 'phags pa rig sngags kyi, "noble... of vidyā-mantras." Its full Sanskrit original is not securely attested, so it is best known by its English rendering. The text is a protective incantation, set as a dialogue in which Daṃṣṭrākarālapiṅgala, the fearsome lord of the bhūtas and…

item.title: The Noble Dhāraṇī of Maṇibhadra (Toh 970)
item.description: The Noble Dhāraṇī of Maṇibhadra, known in Sanskrit as the Āryamaṇibhadranāmadhāraṇī and in Tibetan as Phakpa Norbu Zangpo'i Zung, is a short dhāraṇī scripture set at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, the park of Anāthapiṇḍada, where the Buddha was staying. In it the son of Maṇibhadra, the great general of the yakṣas, approaches the Blessed One and vows to follow closely and serve any monk, nun, layman…
